entities.summary: Simon Bolivar Buckner Jr. was a lieutenant general in the United States Army during World War II who served in the Pacific Theater. As commanding general of Alaska Defense Command, Buckner commanded American-Canadian forces in the Aleutian Islands campaign, including the Battle of Attu and the Kiska Expedition. Following that assignment, he was promoted to command the Tenth Army, which conducted the amphibious invasion of the Japanese island of Okinawa in 1945. He was killed during the closing days of the Battle of Okinawa by enemy artillery fire, making him the highest-ranking United States military officer lost to enemy fire during World War II.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As commanding general of Alaska Defense Command and later Tenth Army, Buckner played a crucial role in the Aleutian Islands campaign and the amphibious invasion of Okinawa, contributing significantly to the Allied victory in World War II. His leadership during these pivotal battles had far-reaching consequences for the Pacific Theater and the ultimate defeat of Japan.
